title: Basic Conv Block: When to use and cautions
text:
Basic Conv Block: When to use and cautions
When to use
• Early and middle stages of almost all CNNs.
• Strong baseline when compute/memory are not tight.
• Good default for feature extraction with stable training recipes.
Cautions
• Parameter/FLOP cost grows quickly with CinCout.
• Repeating only standard conv can be expensive on edge devices.
• Track receptive field and downsampling schedule to avoid over-shrinking.

title: Residual: Cautions in practice
text:
Residual: Cautions in practice
• Shortcut and main branch must have compatible shape before addition.
• Use projection shortcut (1 × 1 conv) when channel count or stride
changes.
• Post-activation vs pre-activation variants behave differently in deep
stacks.
• Residual does not replace proper normalization/regularization design.

title: Residual Block: PyTorch example
text:
Residual Block: PyTorch example
class
ResidualBlock (nn.Module):
def
__init__(self , cin , cout , stride =1):
super ().__init__ ()
self.f = nn.Sequential(
nn.Conv2d(cin , cout , 3, stride=stride , padding =1,
bias=False),
nn.BatchNorm2d(cout), nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
nn.Conv2d(cout , cout , 3, padding =1, bias=False),
nn.BatchNorm2d(cout)
)
self.shortcut = nn.Identity () if (cin == cout and
stride == 1) \
else nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(cin , cout , 1, stride=
stride , bias=False),
nn.BatchNorm2d(cout))
def
forward(self , x):
return F.relu(self.f(x) + self.shortcut(x))

title: Bottleneck: When to use and cautions
text:
Bottleneck: When to use and cautions
When to use
• Deep backbones (ResNet-50/101/152 style).
• High-channel stages where standard 3 × 3 is expensive.
• Scenarios needing deeper networks under a fixed FLOP budget.
Cautions
• If Cmid is too small, representational capacity can bottleneck accuracy.
• Extra 1 × 1 layers add memory access overhead; not always fastest on all
hardware.
• Keep shortcut/projection path design consistent across stages.

Depthwise: Cautions
• Very efficient, but may reduce accuracy if channel mixing is too weak.
• Pointwise (1 × 1) conv still dominates cost at large channel sizes.
• Speedup depends on kernel/runtime support; theoretical FLOP reduction
may not fully translate to wall-clock gain.

DWSeparable(nn.Module):
def
__init__(self , cin , cout):

, bias=False)
self.pw = nn.Conv2d(cin , cout , 1, bias=False)
self.bn = nn.BatchNorm2d(cout)
self.act = nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
def
forward(self , x):
x = self.dw(x)
# spatial
per channel
x = self.pw(x)
# channel
mixing
return
self.act(self.bn(x))

title: Inverted Residual: When to use and cautions
text:
Inverted Residual: When to use and cautions
When to use
• Mobile/edge CNNs where latency and model size are strict constraints.
• Efficient backbones for detection/segmentation on lightweight devices.
• Designs inspired by MobileNetV2/V3 style families.
Cautions
• Expansion ratio too small hurts accuracy; too large hurts latency.
• Keep last projection linear (no activation) to preserve information.
• Skip connection only when stride and channel dimensions match.

title: Inverted Residual: PyTorch example
text:
Inverted Residual: PyTorch example
class
InvertedResidual (nn.Module):
def
__init__(self , cin , cout , expand =6, stride =1):
super ().__init__ ()
cexp = cin * expand
self.block = nn.Sequential(
nn.Conv2d(cin , cexp , 1, bias=False),
nn.BatchNorm2d(cexp), nn.ReLU6(inplace=True),
nn.Conv2d(cexp , cexp , 3, stride=stride , padding =1,
groups=cexp , bias=False),
nn.BatchNorm2d(cexp), nn.ReLU6(inplace=True),
nn.Conv2d(cexp , cout , 1, bias=False),
nn.BatchNorm2d(cout),
)
self.use_skip = (stride == 1 and cin == cout)
def
forward(self , x):
y = self.block(x)
return x + y if self.use_skip
else y

title: SE Block: PyTorch example
text:
SE Block: PyTorch example
class
SEBlock(nn.Module):
def
__init__(self , c, r=16):
super ().__init__ ()
self.pool = nn. AdaptiveAvgPool2d (1)
self.fc = nn.Sequential(
nn.Conv2d(c, c // r, 1), nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
nn.Conv2d(c // r, c, 1), nn.Sigmoid ()
)
def
forward(self , x):
w = self.fc(self.pool(x))
# channel
gates in [0 ,1]
return x * w

SE Block: PyTorch example
class
SEBlock(nn.Module):
def
__init__(self , c, r=16):
super ().__init__ ()
self.pool = nn. AdaptiveAvgPool2d (1)
self.fc = nn.Sequential(
nn.Conv2d(c, c // r, 1), nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
nn.Conv2d(c // r, c, 1), nn.Sigmoid ()
)
def
forward(self , x):
w = self.fc(self.pool(x))
# channel
gates in [0 ,1]
return x * w
